newsitem.title: USA: Plaintiffs value Texaco settlement at $176 mln.
newsitem.headline: Plaintiffs value Texaco settlement at $176 mln.

text.p: The settlement of a race discrimination lawsuit announced by Texaco Inc Friday will cost the company a total of $176 million over five years, lawyers for the plaintiffs said.
Earlier Friday, Texaco said it would make a one-time payment of $115 million, award an 11 percent pay increase and set up four programs to ensure fairness.

Michael Hausfeld, an attorney for the plaintiffs in the case, said at a Washington news conference that the pay increases was for African-American salaried employees and was worth $26.1 million over five years.
The new programs would cost $35 million, Hausfeld said.
"This company has paid the highest amount of any company in a discrimination suit," Hausfeld said.

Attorneys for the six employees who filed the suit in 1994 and the rest of the 1,400 African-Americans who worked for the company from 1991 to the present said the plaintiffs were pleased with the outcome.
"They're ecstatic, and they believe the era of the 'good old boy' network at Texaco is coming to an end," said attorney Cyrus Mehri.
